title: Serialize and deserialize a binary tree
label: idb-list
statement: Design a way to turn a binary tree into a **string** and back again, so that deserialising the string gives back **exactly the same tree** — same shape, same values.
provenance: **InterviewDB-listed.** LeetCode 297 is on the LinkedIn list you supplied from InterviewDB. No candidate report of this exact question was found in the research passes — the evidence is that the list names it. On that list it is a variation of InterviewDB Q17. Q17’s first follow-up, exactly. 297 is the binary case with positional children; Q17 needs keyed children with unique sibling keys, which changes what has to be written: a key per child and a child count or terminator, rather than null markers.

stages.title: Round trip
stages.say: Turn a binary tree into a string, and that string back into the same tree.
stages.require: Implement `TreeCodec.Serialize` and `Deserialize`. Any format, as long as the round trip is exact. Must survive a 100,000-deep tree.

listen: Restates the problem and asks the clarifying questions that change the code (Any format allowed? (Yes — but say why you chose it.); Value range? (Full int, including negatives.))

Reads AI output before running it

1.a: Many shapes share an in-order sequence. Pre-order or level order with null markers is unambiguous.

2.a: O(n) time; the string is O(n).
Binary encoding (varints), or pre-order with a bitmap of which children exist.

4.a: Stream the output to a file node by node; never build the whole string.

5.a: InterviewDB Q17 merges two serialised metadata trees and asks about the format's trade-offs.

prompts.label: Check my design — no code
prompts.text: I believe level order with a marker for each missing child, written and read with the same queue so both directions are iterative — O(n) time and size. Review my reasoning without giving me the implementation. What would break it?

prompts.label: Review, do not rewrite
prompts.text: Review my implementation for correctness and edge cases. Do not rewrite the code. List problems most severe first, each with the input that triggers it.

prompts.label: Race conditions
prompts.text: Now review this implementation for race conditions if multiple threads call Serialize concurrently. For each race, give the interleaving that breaks it. Then name the smallest synchronization boundary that preserves correctness. Do not write code yet.

prompts.label: Tests that expose bugs
prompts.text: Suggest tests that could expose bugs in my implementation: boundaries, duplicates, empty and invalid input, and concurrency where it applies. For each, say why the expected value is correct.

prompts.label: Complexity check
prompts.text: What is the time and space complexity of each public method as written? Do not claim a bound unless every step achieves it.

learn.title: 1 · Problem
learn.md: Design a way to turn a binary tree into a **string** and back again, so that deserialising the string gives back **exactly the same tree** — same shape, same values.

learn.title: 2 · Clarifications
learn.md:
- Any format allowed? (Yes — but say why you chose it.)
- Value range? (Full int, including negatives.)
- How deep can the tree be? (Very — avoid recursion.)

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: Values alone lose the shape; record the gaps too. Level order with a marker for each missing child ("1,2,3,#,#,4,5") can be read back with the same queue that wrote it, and both directions are iterative.

learn.title: 4 · Approach

learn.title: 12 · Common AI mistakes
learn.md:
- Only writing the values (in-order alone cannot rebuild the shape).
- A separator that can appear inside a value (a minus sign is fine; a space-separated format with a "-" marker is not).
- Recursion on a deep tree.
- Ambiguity between an empty tree and a tree with one node of value 0.
